texts.1.1: FROM THE FRENCH OF MADAME DE LA MOTHE GUION. (translated by William Cowper)
texts.1.3: 'Tis folly all--let me no more be told
texts.1.4: Of Parian porticos, and roofs of gold;
texts.1.5: Delightful views of nature, dressed by art,
texts.1.6: Enchant no longer this indifferent heart;
texts.1.7: The Lord of all things, in his humble birth,
texts.1.8: Makes mean the proud magnificence of earth;
texts.1.9: The straw, the manger, and the mouldering wall,
texts.1.10: Eclipse its lustre; and I scorn it all.
texts.1.11: Canals, and fountains, and delicious vales,
texts.1.12: Green slopes and plains, whose plenty never fails;
texts.1.13: Deep-rooted groves, whose heads sublimely rise,
texts.1.14: Earth-born, and yet ambitious of the skies;
texts.1.15: The abundant foliage of whose gloomy shades,
texts.1.16: Vainly the sun in all its power invades;
texts.1.17: Where warbled airs of sprightly birds resound,
texts.1.18: Whose verdure lives while Winter scowls around;
texts.1.19: Rocks, lofty mountains, caverns dark and deep,
texts.1.20: And torrents raving down the rugged steep;
texts.1.21: Smooth downs, whose fragrant herbs the spirits cheer;
texts.1.22: Meads crowned with flowers; streams musical and clear,
texts.1.23: Whose silver waters, and whose murmurs, join
texts.1.24: Their artless charms, to make the scene divine;
texts.1.25: The fruitful vineyard, and the furrowed plain,
texts.1.26: That seems a rolling sea of golden grain:
texts.1.27: All, all have lost the charms they once possessed;
texts.1.28: An infant God reigns sovereign in my breast;
texts.1.29: From Bethlehem's bosom I no more will rove;
texts.1.30: There dwells the Saviour, and there rests my love.
texts.1.31: Ye mightier rivers, that, with sounding force,
texts.1.32: Urge down the valleys your impetuous course!
texts.1.33: Winds, clouds, and lightnings! and, ye waves, whose heads,
texts.1.34: Curled into monstrous forms, the seaman dreads!
texts.1.35: Horrid abyss, where all experience fails,
texts.1.36: Spread with the wreck of planks and shattered sails;
texts.1.37: On whose broad back grim Death triumphant rides,
texts.1.38: While havoc floats on all thy swelling tides,
texts.1.39: Thy shores a scene of ruin strewed around
texts.1.40: With vessels bulged, and bodies of the drowned!
texts.1.41: Ye fish, that sport beneath the boundless waves,
texts.1.42: And rest, secure from man, in rocky caves;
texts.1.43: Swift-darting sharks, and whales of hideous size,
texts.1.44: Whom all the aquatic world with terror eyes!
texts.1.45: Had I but faith immoveable and true,
texts.1.46: I might defy the fiercest storm, like you:
texts.1.47: The world, a more disturbed and boisterous sea,
texts.1.48: When Jesus shows a smile, affrights not me;
texts.1.49: He hides me, and in vain the billows roar,
texts.1.50: Break harmless at my feet, and leave the shore.
texts.1.51: Thou azure vault where, through the gloom of night,
texts.1.52: Thick sown, we see such countless worlds of light!
texts.1.53: Thou moon, whose car, encompassing the skies,
texts.1.54: Restores lost nature to our wondering eyes;
texts.1.55: Again retiring, when the brighter sun
texts.1.56: Begins the course he seems in haste to run!
texts.1.57: Behold him where he shines! His rapid rays,
texts.1.58: Themselves unmeasured, measure all our days;
texts.1.59: Nothing impedes the race he would pursue,
texts.1.61: A thousand lands confess his quickening heat,
texts.1.62: And all he cheers are fruitful, fair, and sweet.
texts.1.63: Far from enjoying what these scenes disclose,
texts.1.64: I feel the thorn, alas! but miss the rose:
texts.1.65: Too well I know this aching heart requires
texts.1.66: More solid gold to fill its vast desires;
texts.1.67: In vain they represent his matchless might,
texts.1.68: Who called them out of deep primeval night;
texts.1.69: Their form and beauty but augment my woe,
texts.1.70: I seek the Giver of those charms they show:
texts.1.71: Nor, Him beside, throughout the world he made,
texts.1.72: Lives there in whom I trust for cure or aid.
texts.1.73: Infinite God, thou great unrivalled One!
texts.1.74: Whose glory makes a blot of yonder sun;
texts.1.75: Compared with thine, how dim his beauty seems,
texts.1.76: How quenched the radiance of his golden beams!
texts.1.77: Thou art my bliss, the light by which I move;
texts.1.78: In thee alone dwells all that I can love.
texts.1.79: All darkness flies when thou art pleased to appear,
texts.1.80: A sudden spring renews the fading year;
texts.1.81: Where'er I turn I see thy power and grace
texts.1.82: The watchful guardians of our heedless race;
texts.1.83: Thy various creatures in one strain agree,
texts.1.84: All, in all times and places, speak of thee;
texts.1.85: E'en I, with trembling heart and stammering tongue,
texts.1.86: Attempt thy praise, and join the general song.
texts.1.87: Almighty Former of this wondrous plan,
texts.1.88: Faintly reflected in thine image, man--
texts.1.89: Holy and just--the greatness of whose name
texts.1.90: Fills and supports this universal frame,
texts.1.91: Diffused throughout the infinitude of space,
texts.1.92: Who art thyself thine own vast dwelling-place;
texts.1.93: Soul of our soul, whom yet no sense of ours
texts.1.94: Discerns, eluding our most active powers;
texts.1.95: Encircling shades attend thine awful throne,
texts.1.96: That veil thy face, and keep thee still unknown;
texts.1.97: Unknown, though dwelling in our inmost part,
texts.1.98: Lord of the thoughts, and Sovereign of the heart!
texts.1.99: Repeat the charming truth that never tires,
texts.1.100: No God is like the God my soul desires;
texts.1.101: He at whose voice heaven trembles, even He,
texts.1.102: Great as he is, knows how to stoop to me--
texts.1.103: Lo! there he lies--that smiling infant said,
texts.1.104: "Heaven, earth, and sea, exist!"--and they obeyed.
texts.1.105: E'en he, whose being swells beyond the skies,
texts.1.106: Is born of woman, lives, and mourns, and dies;
texts.1.107: Eternal and immortal, seems to cast
texts.1.108: That glory from his brows, and breathes his last.
texts.1.109: Trivial and vain the works that man has wrought,
texts.1.110: How do they shrink and vanish at the thought!
texts.1.111: Sweet solitude, and scene of my repose!
texts.1.112: This rustic sight assuages all my woes--
texts.1.113: That crib contains the Lord, whom I adore;
texts.1.114: And earth's a shade that I pursue no more.
texts.1.115: He is my firm support, my rock, my tower,
texts.1.116: I dwell secure beneath his sheltering power,
texts.1.117: And hold this mean retreat for ever dear,
texts.1.118: For all I love, my soul's delight is here.
texts.1.119: I see the Almighty swathed in infant bands,
texts.1.120: Tied helpless down the thunder-bearer's hands!
texts.1.121: And, in this shed, that mystery discern,
texts.1.122: Which faith and love, and they alone, can learn.
texts.1.123: Ye tempests, spare the slumbers of your Lord!
texts.1.124: Ye zephyrs, all your whispered sweets afford!
texts.1.125: Confess the God, that guides the rolling year;
texts.1.126: Heaven, do him homage; and thou, earth, revere!
texts.1.127: Ye shepherds, monarchs, sages, hither bring
texts.1.128: Your hearts an offering, and adore your King!
texts.1.129: Pure be those hearts, and rich in faith and love;
texts.1.130: Join, in his praise, the harmonious world above;
texts.1.131: To Bethlehem haste, rejoice in his repose,
texts.1.132: And praise him there for all that he bestows!
texts.1.133: Man, busy man, alas! can ill afford
texts.1.134: To obey the summons, and attend the Lord;
texts.1.135: Perverted reason revels and runs wild,
texts.1.136: By glittering shows of pomp and wealth beguiled;
texts.1.137: And, blind to genuine excellence and grace,
texts.1.138: Finds not her author in so mean a place.
texts.1.139: Ye unbelieving! learn a wiser part,
texts.1.140: Distrust your erring sense, and search your heart;
texts.1.141: There soon ye shall perceive a kindling flame
texts.1.142: Glow for that infant God, from whom it came;
texts.1.143: Resist not, quench not, that divine desire,
texts.1.144: Melt all your adamant in heavenly fire!
texts.1.145: Not so will I requite thee, gentle love!
texts.1.146: Yielding and soft this heart shall ever prove;
texts.1.147: And every heart beneath thy power should fall,
texts.1.148: Glad to submit, could mine contain them all.
texts.1.149: But I am poor, oblation I have none,
texts.1.150: None for a Saviour, but himself alone:
texts.1.151: Whate'er I render thee, from thee it came:
texts.1.152: And, if I give my body to the flame,
texts.1.153: My patience, love, and energy divine
texts.1.154: Of heart, and soul, and spirit, all are thine.
texts.1.155: Ah, vain attempt to expunge the mighty score!
texts.1.156: The more I pay, I owe thee still the more.
texts.1.157: Upon my meanness, poverty, and guilt,
texts.1.158: The trophy of thy glory shall be built;
texts.1.159: My self-disdain shall be the unshaken base,
texts.1.160: And my deformity its fairest grace;
texts.1.161: For destitute of good, and rich in ill,
texts.1.162: Must be my state and my description still.
texts.1.163: And do I grieve at such an humbling lot?
texts.1.164: Nay, but I cherish and enjoy the thought--
texts.1.165: Vain pageantry and pomp of earth, adieu!
texts.1.166: I have no wish, no memory for you;
texts.1.167: The more I feel my misery, I adore
texts.1.168: The sacred inmate of my soul the more;
texts.1.169: Rich in his love, I feel my noblest pride
texts.1.170: Spring from the sense of having nought beside.
texts.1.171: In thee I find wealth, comfort, virtue, might;
texts.1.172: My wanderings prove thy wisdom infinite;
texts.1.173: All that I have I give thee; and then see
texts.1.175: For thou hast joined them, taking up our woe,
texts.1.176: And pouring out thy bliss on worms below,
texts.1.177: By filling with thy grace and love divine
texts.1.178: A gulf of evil in this heart of mine.
texts.1.179: This is, indeed, to bid the valleys rise,
texts.1.180: And the hills sink--'tis matching earth and skies;
texts.1.181: I feel my weakness, thank thee and deplore
texts.1.182: An aching heart, that throbs to thank thee more;
texts.1.183: The more I love thee, I the more reprove
texts.1.184: A soul so lifeless, and so slow to love;
texts.1.185: Till, on a deluge of thy mercy tossed,
texts.1.186: I plunge into that sea, and there am lost.
texts.1.187: God Neither Known nor Loved by the World
texts.1.188: Ye linnets, let us try, beneath this grove,
texts.1.189: Which shall be loudest in our Maker's praise!
texts.1.190: In quest of some forlorn retreat I rove,
texts.1.191: For all the world is blind, and wanders from his ways.
texts.1.192: That God alone should prop the sinking soul,
texts.1.193: Fills them with rage against his empire now:
texts.1.194: I traverse earth in vain from pole to pole,
texts.1.195: To seek one simple heart, set free from all below.
texts.1.196: They speak of love, yet little feel its sway,
texts.1.197: While in their bosom many an idol lurks;
texts.1.198: Their base desires, well satisfied, obey,
texts.1.199: Leave the Creator's hand, and lean upon his works.
texts.1.200: 'Tis therefore I can dwell with man no more;
texts.1.201: Your fellowship, ye warblers! suits me best:
texts.1.202: Pure love has lost its price, though prized of yore,
texts.1.203: Profaned by modern tongues, and slighted as a jest.
texts.1.204: My God, who formed you for his praise alone,
texts.1.205: Beholds his purpose well fulfilled in you;
texts.1.206: Come, let us join the choir before his throne,
texts.1.207: Partaking in his praise with spirits just and true.
texts.1.208: Yes, I will always love; and, as I ought,
texts.1.209: Tune to the praise of love my ceaseless voice;
texts.1.210: Preferring love too vast for human thought,
texts.1.211: In spite of erring men, who cavil at my choice.
texts.1.212: Why have I not a thousand thousand hearts,
texts.1.213: Lord of my soul! that they might all be thine?
texts.1.214: If thou approve--the zeal thy smile imparts,
texts.1.215: How should it ever fail! can such a fire decline?
texts.1.216: Love, pure and holy, is a deathless fire;
texts.1.217: Its object heavenly, it must ever blaze:
texts.1.218: Eternal love a God must needs inspire,
texts.1.219: When once he wins the heart, and fits it for his praise.
texts.1.220: Self-love dismissed--'tis then we live indeed--
texts.1.221: In her embrace, death, only death is found:
texts.1.222: Come, then, one noble effort, and succeed,
texts.1.223: Cast off the chain of self with which thy soul is bound.
texts.1.224: Oh! I could cry, that all the world might hear,
texts.1.225: Ye self-tormentors, love your God alone;
texts.1.226: Let his unequalled excellence be dear,
texts.1.227: Dear to your inmost souls, and make him all your own!
texts.1.228: They hear me not--alas! how fond to rove
texts.1.229: In endless chase of folly's specious lure!
texts.1.230: 'Tis here alone, beneath this shady grove,
texts.1.231: I taste the sweets of truth--here only am secure.
texts.1.233: I am fond of the swallow--I learn from her flight,
texts.1.234: Had I skill to improve it, a lesson of love:
texts.1.235: How seldom on earth do we see her alight!
texts.1.236: She dwells in the skies, she is ever above.
texts.1.237: It is on the wing that she takes her repose,
texts.1.238: Suspended and poised in the regions of air,
texts.1.239: 'Tis not in our fields that her sustenance grows,
texts.1.240: It is winged like herself--'tis ethereal fare.
texts.1.241: She comes in the spring, all the summer she stays,
texts.1.242: And, dreading the cold, still follows the sun--
texts.1.243: So, true to our love, we should covet his rays,
texts.1.244: And the place where he shines not immediately shun.
texts.1.245: Our light should be love, and our nourishment prayer;
texts.1.246: It is dangerous food that we find upon earth;
texts.1.247: The fruit of this world is beset with a snare,
texts.1.248: In itself it is hurtful, as vile in its birth.
texts.1.249: 'Tis rarely, if ever, she settles below,
texts.1.250: And only when building a nest for her young;
texts.1.251: Were it not for her brood, she would never bestow
texts.1.252: A thought upon anything filthy as dung.
texts.1.253: Let us leave it ourselves ('tis a mortal abode),
texts.1.254: To bask every moment in infinite love;
texts.1.255: Let us fly the dark winter, and follow the road
texts.1.256: That leads to the dayspring appearing above.

texts.1.258: Ah! reign, wherever man is found!
texts.1.260: Then I am rich, and I abound,
texts.1.261: When every human heart is thine.
texts.1.262: A thousand sorrows pierce my soul,
texts.1.263: To think that all are not thine own:
texts.1.264: Ah! be adored from pole to pole;
texts.1.265: Where is thy zeal? arise; be known!
texts.1.266: All hearts are cold, in every place,
texts.1.267: Yet earthly good with warmth pursue;
texts.1.268: Dissolve them with a flash of grace,
texts.1.269: Thaw these of ice, and give us new!
